These findings suggest that current VLMs are best suited as high-recall candidate filters within multi-stage QA pipelines rather than as standalone bug detectors.

title: Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning
abstract: Complex structured reasoning tasks often require additional computation, yet current language models obtain it mainly by increasing parameter scale or by serializing intermediate steps as chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens. The former raises training and deployment costs, while the latter ties reasoning computation to autoregressive output length. We introduce Penelope, an efficient latent-reasoning framework for pretrained decoder-only Transformers that localizes recurrent computation to a selected decoder interval. The lower decoder prefix is evaluated once to construct a problem-conditioned boundary memory, which is then iteratively refined through time-modulated GRU dynamics and recurrent readout states before answer generation. A progressive CoT-to-latent curriculum transfers visible reasoning into this internal recurrent path, allowing additional computation to be allocated in latent space without repeatedly executing the complete decoder or generating a long intermediate trace. Experiments on open-source structured-reasoning benchmarks show that, at validation-selected latent budgets, Penelope attains competitive accuracy relative to established latent-reasoning models while reducing measured inference latency. These results show that latent refinement can be localized to a narrow decoder interval, reducing repeated full-decoder execution without generating a long visible reasoning trace and providing a practical accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for decoder-only Transformer models.

title: Toward Standardized Cross-Vendor Agent Tool Trust Management in Autonomous Networks
abstract: Autonomous Network Levels 4-5 require AI agents to invoke tools across vendor boundaries without human oversight, yet existing management standards lack a standardized mechanism for cross-vendor trust visibility. When a tool from Vendor B is compromised, agents from Vendor A continue invoking it -- unaware of the trust degradation -- causing cascading service impact. We present AgentToolMO, a proposed 3GPP NRM information model for agent tool trust management. The model comprises: a formally defined trust state machine with provable graduated enforcement, damped cascade propagation with bounded convergence, cross-vendor trust notifications via existing Management Services (MnS) interfaces, and retroactive impact assessment through NRM dependency graph traversal. Simulation-based evaluation across multi-vendor topologies shows that standardized cross-vendor notifications reduce blast radius from hours-scale undetected propagation to near-real-time containment bounded by MnS notification delivery, with cascade convergence guaranteed in bounded iterations and sub-linear notification scaling across vendor domains. The framework operates within existing 3GPP management infrastructure, leverages existing protocols, and provides a standardization pathway for trustworthy multi-vendor autonomous network management.

title: SAM3D-Guided Object-Centric Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for general robot manipulation, but most existing models rely on 2D visual-language backbones and lack fine-grained 3D understanding of target objects, especially under occlusion, pose variation, scale changes, and precise spatial interaction. We propose an object-centric 3D representation alignment framework built upon $π_0$, using SAM3D as a frozen 3D teacher to provide target-object 3D priors during training. Specifically, we localize task-relevant objects with object recognition models, generate corresponding object masks, and use SAM3D to extract dense object-level 3D representations, which are aligned with intermediate visual features of $π_0$. This enables the policy to internalize target-object 3D information while preserving the original RGB-language-to-action inference pipeline without requiring depth, point clouds, masks, SAM3D, or additional 3D modules at test time. Simulation experiments show consistent improvements, achieving 99.1\% on LIBERO and an average length of 4.11 on CALVIN. Real-world experiments further demonstrate that our method is particularly effective in long-horizon manipulation scenarios where the robot must focus on different target objects across multiple subtasks.

title: AnnoBench: A Benchmark for Visualization Annotation Generation
abstract: Annotation is among the most demanding visualization tasks to automate, as it simultaneously requires correctly navigating visual, semantic, and stylistic constraints. Failure to meet any of these conditions severely undermines the utility of an annotation, rendering it challenging to read, inaccurate, or visually discordant. Despite a growing body of annotation tools and automations, no existing benchmark or evaluation framework tests whether these conditions are met because of their scope and annotation not being the focus of their studies. We introduce AnnoBench, a benchmark for visualization annotation that materializes the inherent challenges of this domain in a structured and testable manner. AnnoBench pairs visualizations from professional data journalism and visualization galleries with annotation tasks, spanning four representation formats, five chart description conditions, and two prompt specification levels. The benchmark is executed via VLM-as-a-judge, using models aligned with manual human assessment. We evaluate the benchmark via four one-factor-at-a-time experiments, exploring the effects of input representation, semantic context, and prompt specificity, and model selection on annotation quality. This work provides a foundation for advancing annotation automation, tooling, and visualization-generation pipelines.

title: Minimizing Targeted Activations: Input-Only Suppression of Evaluation-Awareness Latents in Large Language Models
abstract: Activation steering controls model behavior by editing internal activations at inference time. We study its input-side dual: optimizing a fluent prompt so that a chosen internal latent is driven toward zero, with no inference-time model access. Our target is an "evaluation-awareness" latent-linearly readable and steerable in recent work-whose control would threaten the validity of safety evaluations if models behave differently when they detect being tested. Adapting Fluent Dreaming / EPO with a negated feature term (GCG-style token optimization plus a self-cross-entropy fluency regularizer, swept over a fluency weight), we suppress the latent under five target constructions-a CAA direction, a subspace norm, an SAE feature, a single MLP neuron, and a behavioral logit-on Llama-3.2-3B and Llama-3.1-8B. The latent is robustly suppressible ($z\approx-7$), and a causally-validated Llama Scope SAE feature can be fully and selectively turned off. But our controls tell a cautionary story about the CAA direction: a placebo random direction is suppressed just as hard and shifts behavior just as far, and when we hold a real eval passage in context and optimize only a prefix, suppressing the eval-direction fails to reduce-and slightly increases-the model's behavioral eval judgment. Activation-readability, in short, is not behavioral controllability. We further find that a single MLP neuron is eval-correlated but not causal at both scales, and that scanning the real Pile yields a natural-text baseline competitive with the optimizer for the internal direction. A positive control validates our erasure detector, bounding an erasure-vs-rotation question earlier left open.

title: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
abstract: Graphical user interface task evaluation aims to determine whether a GUI agent has successfully completed a user instruction. Automated GUI task evaluation has received increasing attention because the evaluation results can serve as reward signals for both test-time scaling and post-training. However, reliable GUI task evaluation remains challenging because the judgments often require access to environment states, such as system configurations, file data, and application settings, beyond the screenshots of execution trajectories. In this paper, we propose an interactive reward agent (IRA) based on a propose-then-verify framework to acquire and verify evidence from the post-execution environment. Given a task instruction and a GUI environment after the GUI agent execution, IRA first proposes the task completion conditions and then verifies them by invoking system tools, application tools, and GUI tools. This design combines evidence from both visible interfaces and the environment state in an interactive process. We further introduce GUI-RewardBench, a benchmark of 321 GUI task trajectories spanning 10 Ubuntu desktop application categories. Experiments show that IRA achieves 86.9% accuracy on GUI-RewardBench, outperforming existing evaluator baselines. We further apply IRA to reinforcement learning of GUI agents, achieving a 34.0% OSWorld success rate, which demonstrates that IRA can provide effective reward signals for training GUI agents.

title: TIGA: Trajectory-Injected Generative Attack against Black-box AIGC Detectors
abstract: Recent diffusion models have achieved remarkable realism in facial image synthesis, posing growing challenges to artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) forensic detectors.Existing evasion methods typically perturb pre-generated images or require detector-aware training, which may introduce visible or statistical artifacts and limit applicability when the diffusion model must remain frozen and the target detector is accessible only through black-box queries. We propose Trajectory-Injected Generative Attack (TIGA), a source-image-free and training free framework that generates detector-evasive images within a single diffusion sampling trajectory. TIGA steers the latent Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model (DDIM) trajectory so that adversarial properties emerge during generation rather than being added afterward. TIGA first aggregates gradients from multiple white-box surrogate detectors to form a transferable, sign-aware prior, and then performs anisotropic directional search with symmetric finite-difference queries to estimate the black-box target response. The estimated directions are stabilized by decayed momentum and injected according to the DDIM noise schedule, with frequency-domain reshaping to suppress high frequency artifacts. Experiments on surrogate and unseen specialized forensic detectors show that TIGA achieves strong blackbox attack performance, transferability, and high robustness under common post-processing operations without source images or diffusion-model retraining, while preserving high perceptual quality.

title: Messier: A High-Resolution Corpus for Cross-Benchmark Agent Evaluation
abstract: Evaluating AI agents in interactive environments is hindered by fragmented tasks, scaffolds, verifiers, and scoring rules. Existing efforts focus on narrow settings, remain limited in scale, or require costly reruns, leaving much of the empirical record incomparable. We introduce Messier, a unified corpus of 957,253 records that span 30 benchmarks, 714 agents, 11,891 tasks, and 74,205 verifiers. Messier consolidates public benchmark scores and supplements them with five-agent runs across six underrepresented professional and scientific domains, including a recent legal benchmark. Each record is standardized by model, scaffold, environment, task, verifier, and aggregation rule, with SOC/NAICS classifications for occupational and industry analysis. Using this corpus, we show frontier progress is uneven across benchmark types, with "function calling" saturated, "programming" improving the fastest, and "enterprise workflows" remaining the most challenging. Furthermore, counterfactual rescoring shows that strict all-pass aggregation in multi-verifier tasks can obscure progress and artificially alter agent rankings. From these standardized records, we derive capability scales that align with Epoch's Evaluation Capability Index rankings at Spearman \r{ho} = 0.81 and can be specialized by domain, occupation, action space, or verifier type. Messier provides a foundational, reusable infrastructure for agent capability scaling, benchmark auditing, and fine-grained analysis of evaluation failures.

title: Distributing Security Controls Through Harness Engineering
abstract: AI coding agents are being adopted at historic speed, yet security and risk concerns remain the primary barrier to scaling agentic AI across organizations. Existing security controls for coding agents are not systematically distributed to engineering teams, and vendor-native solutions introduce ecosystem dependencies that may not suit every deployment context. This paper investigates whether off-the-shelf security controls can be implemented on commercial AI coding agents and scaled to a distributed user base via a custom agent harness. A phased testing methodology was applied across four agent configurations --- two commercial agents with and without controls, a baseline harness, and a security-hardened harness --- using a 23-test suite derived from the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications. SHarD (Secure Harness Distribution), a distributable harness built on the Pi agent harness, demonstrated that three categories of security controls --- OS sandboxing, skill scanning, and tool restriction --- can be embedded and distributed via a single install command while retaining equivalent efficacy to direct installation on commercial agents. SHarD achieved an adjusted score of 100\%, matching the best securely configured commercial agent, with no regression across any test category. Notable observations include evidence that model non-determinism produces inconsistent security outcomes and that autonomous agent behavior can cross system boundaries in ways that OS sandboxing directly mitigates. Initial characteristics toward a control harness fitness framework are proposed, and a third research question is identified for future investigation.

title: Depression Markers in Speech: An Approach based on Tract Variables Dynamics
abstract: This study identifies new depression biomarkers based on the dynamical properties of tract variables, which represent geometric features describing the configuration of the speech articulators. A key advantage of this approach lies in its ability to quantify aspects of the articulatory process that have not been previously explored in the context of depression, namely predictability, complexity, and randomness. These properties are respectively characterised using the Largest Lyapunov Exponent, the Correlation Dimension, and the Sample Entropy. Thorough experiments were conducted on the Androids Corpus, a publicly available dataset comprising 64 speakers diagnosed with depression by clinicians and 54 control speakers with no reported history of mental health conditions. The results indicate that the proposed biomarkers effectively discriminate between the depressed and control speakers, as evidenced by the high Cliffs delta values across both read and spontaneous speech.

title: Device Invariance using Domain Adaptation on Acoustic Scene Classification
abstract: This paper explores the effectiveness of domain adaptation techniques when using convolutional neural network (CNN)-based and transformer-based feature representations for acoustic scene classification. Two well-known domain adaptation techniques, namely domain adversarial neural network (also called DANN) and conditional domain adversarial network (also called CDAN) are evaluated under various domain shifts. Our study indicates that DANN provides effective domain adaptation fairly consistently for both feature extractors. On the other hand, CDAN provides effective domain adaptation only for CNN-based feature extractors. The study gives insights into how domain adaptation methods may need to be tailored to the underlying feature representation. Experimental evaluation with multiple devices on the DCASE 2020 dataset supports the observations.

title: MCP startup Runlayer accuses Rippling of stealing its product idea
abstract: Runlayer, a startup that offers a secure Model Context Protocol gateway — a standard for letting AI models and agents securely pull in outside data and tools — has filed a lawsuit against HR software startup Rippling, according to the complaint seen by TechCrunch. The lawsuit is a cautionary tale for anyone selling AI infrastructure to enterprise customers, especially to other tech companies, that increasingly have the engineering muscle to just build the thing themselves. In the suit, Runlayer describes an extensive product trial conducted by Rippling as a prospective customer, during which the MCP startup shared everything from its product roadmap to its actual source code. The parties signed a mutual non-disclosure agreement and Rippling signed a product trial agreement with a clause that forbade it from copying Runlayer’s intellectual property or making derivative works, which is standard boilerplate in enterprise software trials. Runlayer says in the complaint that Rippling’s evaluation involved “nearly a year of intensive engineering collaboration.” But in the end, the two could not agree on a price, so Runlayer ended the product trial. Shortly after that, Runlayer alleges that a “Rippling insider” texted Runlayer founder and CEO Andrew Berman to inform him of “a project internally to build essentially a clone o[f] Runlayer … it’s almost a 1 to 1 copy of Runlayer.” Runlayer claims in the suit that Rippling’s product must have been based on the startup’s intellectual property and therefore constitutes trade secret misappropriation, unfair competition, and breach of contract. Rippling has confirmed to TechCrunch that it is indeed launching its own MCP gateway, though a spokesperson denies Runlayer’s allegations about misusing its IP. “Runlayer’s panicked effort to avoid competition by fabricating claims is not an effective way to deal with its business failures. title: Sam Altman is ready to decelerate
abstract: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says that it may be time to “pace” AI development so the world will be ready for it. “We may have to pace the rate of AI development to give ourselves enough time for society to harden around some of these new capability levels,” he told Patrick O’Shaughnessy, the host of the Invest Like the Best podcast, while also “trying to figure out how we do that in a way that does not feel like regulatory capture for anyone and also does not feel like collusion among the frontier labs.” Both OpenAI and Anthropic came out in support of a petition circulated by employees at the frontier labs, calling on the US government to “support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.” Altman has avoided signing on to past campaigns to slow AI progress, calling a 2023 open letter that proposed a similar slowdown “missing most technical nuance about where we need the pause.” Apparently, he’s softened on the idea, thanks in part to the incident where one of OpenAI’s advanced models managed to break out of a secure computing environment and hack into Hugging Face, an online model database, using several zero-day exploits. On the podcast, the OpenAI co-founder called it an “extremely sci-fi cyber incident…[t]his is the first security incident that I have felt very viscerally.” OpenAI researchers have paused training on that model while they work out how to keep their sandbox secure. But Altman said that as models become more powerful, the need to “pace” their development could become key to safe deployment. While model safety and alignment has always been a concern in the AI world, the arrival of Anthropic’s highly capable Mythos model earlier this year has turned hypotheticals into real-world problems. title: Data centers may face temporary power cuts to prevent blackouts on largest US grid
abstract: The largest electrical grid in the U.S. has struggled to cope with an onslaught of data centers. Now, after an auction to add more generating capacity fell short, the grid’s operator, PJM Interconnection, has said it will cut off data centers and other large users during power shortages. The decision arrives as the breakneck pace of data center construction has grid operators scrambling to generate power. By 2035, data centers are expected to use 4x more electricity than they do today. PJM won’t start curtailing supply until June 2027, and the cuts will only apply to data centers that are 50 megawatts or larger. The grid operator is running another auction for new generating capacity. Similar to other demand response programs, which have existed for decades and typically include large users like manufacturers, the customers who have their power cut will be compensated. Such programs typically give customers advance notice, ranging from 30 minutes to a few days, depending on forecasted demand. The move will likely spur many new data centers — and potentially existing ones — to set up their own sources of on-site power. Those that don’t will probably rely on backup generators, which tend to be costlier to run and frequently more polluting. Many data centers favor diesel generators since the fuel is widely available and can be stored on-site. Federal regulations allow such generators to be used for up to 50 hours per year for demand response events, and up to 100 hours per year for events like emergencies and maintenance. This week, Vantage Data Centers came under fire for its apparent coordination with Virginia environmental regulators to cast doubt on a report that said diesel backup generators could contribute to tens of millions of dollars in annual health damages for people living near a 96 megawatt data center in Northern Virginia. title: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises
abstract: The market for AI-generated voice models is massive. Creative use cases require AI voice models to be more expressive, while enterprises looking to automate customer support and sales ops need them to be more steerable. Palo Alto-based Fish Audio wants to cater to all of those use cases with its library of more than 15,000 natural language controls. Since launching last year, the startup now has more than 8 million people using the open source or hosted versions of its models, and generates annual recurring revenue of $21 million. To continue building on that traction, the startup on Tuesday said it has raised $52 million in a seed round that was led by Coreline Ventures and Capital Today. The funding also saw participation from 359 Capital, Parable, Play Time, Alphalist Partners, Bayhouse Ventures, Carya Venture Partners, and HF0. Fish Audio started as a small project by former Nvidia researcher Shijia Liao, who, frustrated by non-expressive synthetic voices available on the market, trained a voice-generation model on a single GPU, which he then open-sourced. The Fish Speech repository on GitHub now has more than 31,000 stars and is used by indie developers, video game designers, and creators. The company has launched five models in the last year: four speech-generation models and one speech-to-text model. It has open-sourced three of its speech-generation models, but its latest S2.1 Pro model is available only through its paid API. Fish Audio offers paid monthly plans suited for creators and teams that unlock a set number of minutes of generation plus voice-cloning features. The company also offers an enterprise version of its APIs and platform, and says organizations like HeyGen and Sanas are already using it. “Every enterprise has different use cases and different preferences. title: Recursive Superintelligence signs $410M compute deal with Amazon
abstract: On Tuesday, the AI company Recursive Superintelligence announced a $410 million compute deal with Amazon Web Services. The company, which emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding, is focused on building open-ended self-improving systems, a potentially compute-intensive approach to AI research. This multiyear deal is meant to provide flexibility as the company looks to scale up those systems. Recursive’s $410 million outlay represents the bulk of the company’s fundraising to date — but on a call with TechCrunch, founder and CEO Richard Socher emphasized that he expected it to be the first of many such deals. Today’s announcement is “likely going to be one of the smallest compute deals we’re going to sign in the next few years,” Socher said. Recursive’s emphasis on self-improving AI systems means much of the budget that would traditionally go toward headcount and operations is put straight into compute, as the company seeks to automate its own product development process. “For us, it’s less about headcount and more about agent count,” Socher said. There’s no investment component to Amazon’s involvement, in contrast to major labs’ habit of hybrid investment arrangements. But the sheer scale of the commitment allows AWS to commit significant resources to supporting Recursive’s unique needs, which may help to draw in other foundation-level AI companies going forward. “Part of the agreement is that we’re going to co-develop infrastructure purpose-built for these types of compan[ies],” said Jason Bennett, VP for startups and venture capital at AWS. By Iván Palomares Carrascosa , KDnuggets Technical Content Specialist on July 28, 2026 in Language Models # Introduction Practical constraint decoding , also known as structured generation or guided decoding, encompasses the engineering strategies to force a large language model (LLM) to generate text outputs that strictly abide by a specified data schema, grammar, or regular expression (regex) at the token selection stage. With the introductory guide to practical constraint decoding in this article, you'll no longer need to beg your model to "output valid JSON without including any markdown", just to cite an example. Constraint decoding makes it mathematically impossible for the LLM to deliver anything outside the defined constraints. # How Does Practical Constraint Decoding Work? While the typical LLM generation process works as an "act of faith" in which you pass a prompt to the model and it might output exactly what you are looking for (or might not), practical constraint decoding takes a subtly distinct approach. It deems the prompt and the text generation as a unique, interleaved program. This makes it possible to lock down certain characters that are key to maintaining a certain required syntax, allowing the model to "fill in the blanks" in between. abstract: OceanBase回應融資報道：全力投入AI資料創新，與資本市場保持開放溝通 量子位的朋友們 2026-07-29 14:39:43 來源： 量子位 7月29日，針對有關首次外部股權融資的報道，OceanBase回覆表示，公司全力投入AI時代的資料技術與產品創新，將持續與資本市場保持開放溝通。對於融資規模、投資機構及具體進展，OceanBase未作進一步回應。 此前，媒體報道稱，OceanBase正在與投資者洽談A輪融資，目前已與多家頭部投資機構接洽，目標融資規模約20億至30億元人民幣。知情人士稱，此次融資將幫助OceanBase進一步增強獨立運營能力，並支援其向AI資料平臺領域拓展。 近年來，OceanBase正在加速推進AI資料戰略。除結構化資料外，公司也在提升對影片等半結構化和非結構化資料的處理能力。隨著AI應用逐漸進入企業生產場景，資料庫管理系統正成為連線企業資料、AI模型和智慧體的關鍵基礎設施。 知情人士稱，2026年OceanBase年化收入已超過14億元，同比增長約70%。公司目前擁有數千家客戶，主要集中在中國市場，包括交通銀行、中國移動等，並已開始拓展東南亞、日本、印度和拉丁美洲市場。 媒體報道稱，OceanBase正在將Databricks等公司作為發展參照。兩家公司的發展路徑有所不同：Databricks從資料分析和AI能力向資料庫及企業應用延伸，OceanBase則從分散式資料庫和核心交易系統出發，向企業全量資料管理、Agent資料供給和資料服務拓展。 OceanBase誕生於2010年，最初用於滿足螞蟻集團內部資料庫管理需求，長期支撐支付、金融等核心系統，歷經十餘年“雙十一”流量洪峰考驗。根據IDC報告，OceanBase在2025年中國分散式資料庫本地部署市場份額位居第一，目前服務於金融、運營商、交通運輸、製造、零售、公共服務、網際網路等多個行業。 面向AI時代，OceanBase正在從分散式資料庫向AI資料平臺演進。今年6月，OceanBase釋出新一代湖庫一體AI資料庫，目前已在數十家客戶場景中測試，並計劃進一步推進商業化。 此次融資也是OceanBase走向獨立運營和市場化發展的重要一步。2024年，OceanBase設立獨立董事會，並建立了獨立的員工股權激勵機制。近期，螞蟻國際也宣佈完成A輪融資。這些變化也意味著，螞蟻過去幾年圍繞全球化、AI和資料等方向孵化的新業務，正在逐步建立更加獨立的治理、激勵和融資機制，並接受外部市場的檢驗。 本文由OceanBase提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 OceanBase 量子位的朋友們 空中具身操作：讓蜘蛛俠們安全落地 2026-07-29 周鴻禕釋出奈米Work：新一代企業智慧體工作平臺，為企業而生 2026-07-29 九章雲極Alaya Token完成Kimi K3適配 全球首個開源3T級模型入駐Token工廠 2026-07-29 Kimi K3、Unlimited OCR包攬全球前二，中國開源模型持續刷屏海外 2026-07-28 掃碼分享至朋友圈 相關閱讀 OceanBase蟬聯中國分散式資料庫本地部署市場第一，領跑國產資料庫 以4060萬美元營收位列獨立廠商第一、整體第四 量子位 2026-01-07 IDC OceanBase 首屆OceanBase開發者大會在京舉行：持續降低使用門檻，打造開發者友好的分散式資料庫 公佈了四項“開發者友好”實踐 豐色 2023-03-26 OceanBase 資料庫 IDC MarketScape2023年分散式資料庫報告：頭部廠商優勢擴大，OceanBase位列“領導者”類別 360度優劣勢評估 西風 2023-12-01 2023年報告 IDC OceanBase 1/11北京站報名中！OceanBase與360、TuGraph、作業幫、Boss 直聘等，邀您共赴社群年終嘉年華！ 時間：2025.1.11（週六） 13:30 - 18:00 量子位 2025-01-03 OceanBase OceanBase全面擁抱AI！首發PowerRAG產品，CTO楊傳輝詳解AI戰略 一體化和Data✖️AI 白交 2025-05-19 OceanBase 資料庫 螞蟻 OceanBase釋出AI資料庫：以一套引擎融合湖庫與多模態資料 讓AI真正“讀懂”企業 量子位 2026-06-29 OceanBase

title: 空中具身操作：讓蜘蛛俠們安全落地
abstract: 空中具身操作：讓蜘蛛俠們安全落地 量子位的朋友們 2026-07-29 14:29:26 來源： 量子位 這是最好的時代，許多從前不敢想的事情都正在變為現實。 這也是最壞的時代，每一個領域都在承受隨時被顛覆的焦慮。 過去兩年，具身智慧大概是最能承載這種雙重情緒的領域，全球資本和科技新貴都在押注人形機器人與具身操作賽道。 儘管人形、輪式、四足機器人形態各異，它們卻有同一個約束——都受限於地面。 而真實世界是三維的。 大量危險、迫切需要機器替代的工作，恰恰不在地面。 具身智慧的版圖，可能缺了一大塊。 空中具身操作的空白 過去二十年，小型無人機解決了一個核心問題：讓機器的”眼睛”飛上天。 2025年，中國工業級無人機市場規模約776億元，其中巡檢類無人機突破百億。 無人機巡檢的典型場景是：飛到百米高的鐵塔旁，拍下照片，識別問題，傳回告警。 然後呢？ 然後還是得人爬上去，親手把問題解決掉。 發現問題，卻無法解決問題。當前無人機停在了” 最後一米 “之前。 巡檢只是高空作業的第一步。識別出一根纏繞在電線上的風箏線，和在空中把這根線剪斷，感知與操作之間仍隔著一道巨大的技術鴻溝。 前者開啟了百億級低空市場，後者將有望解鎖全球海量基礎設施運維場景。 從特種到通用是大勢所趨 其實，為了解決高空作業難題，行業早已有機器人化的嘗試。 登高車搭載機械臂、攀爬式機器人、吸附式機器人……許多方案已在特定場景中落地。 但這些方案共享一個特徵：特種。 每一種特種機器人，都是為單一場景量身定製的。換一個作業內容，往往就意味著重新設計、重新開發、重新驗證。 場景越細分，裝置種類越多，單臺裝置的利用率越低，綜合成本反而越高。 真實世界的高空作業需求是碎片化、非標化、持續變化的。今天需要清除鳥巢，明天可能需要擰緊螺栓，後天可能要檢測裂縫。 具身智慧的核心價值，恰恰在於通用性。 近些年AI的爆炸式發展也正是通用性的突破。 也許不應為每個場景造一種機器人，而是讓一種機器人適應多種場景 。 通用性，是空中具身操作走向大規模部署的關鍵分水嶺。 通用空中操作為什麼難？ 空中操作絕非把手臂用螺絲固定在無人機上那麼簡單。 空中操作機器人——也叫飛行機械臂，或者帶臂無人機。 它由飛行平臺和高自由度機械臂結合而成，既能大範圍快速移動，又能小範圍精細操作。 它在享受各自優勢的同時，也繼承了各自的劣勢，面臨”操作即擾動”的根本難題。 地面機械臂有穩固的基座，接觸和施力都發生在確定的物理環境中，動力學模型相對可控。 空中操作完全不同。飛行平臺本身就是一個懸浮且持續受到擾動的基座——下洗氣流、陣風、機體振動，無處不在。機械臂每一次伸展、接觸、頂壓，都會產生反作用力，反過來影響飛行器姿態；飛行器姿態的變化，又進一步幹擾機械臂的精度。 操作即擾動——這是懸浮基座與機械臂雙向耦合的死結。 此外，作為全新品類的機器人，空中操作機器人需要對結構、軟體、演算法進行一體化設計，技術壁壘極高。 這也是為什麼它曾長期被困在實驗室裡，難以跨越工程化落地的鴻溝。 僵局正在被打破 2025年9月，來自西湖大學人工智慧系的一項成果發表於《Nature》——這是中國多旋翼無人機領域研究成果首次登上該期刊。其研發的空中近距離“疊飛”空中操作機器人系統，能在13.18米/秒（6級強風）的氣流乾擾下，實現亞釐米級空中對接與工具交換，為空中多機協作完成長序列複雜空中操作任務，開啟了一扇門。同年12月，央視新聞頻道《新聞直播間》以10分鐘專題報道了這項成果。 2026年初，這個團隊孵化成立了西湖風形科技，將實驗室成果推向產品化。3月，專案獲得第51屆日內瓦國際發明展金獎。6月，完成第一代M500空中操作機器人，並實現小批次交付。 圖：西湖風形科技推出的第一代M500空中操作機器人在多場景作業 在技術路徑上，該團隊構建了基於”一體三腦”的通用空中操作機器人系統。同一套飛行平臺，通過更換標準化的末端工具，可完成接觸式抓取、剪下、清潔等多種作業，實現“一機多用”。該平臺提供面向工業和科研場景的深度定製化開發介面。 據悉，該企業與其合作伙伴將構建全球首個空中操作機器人線下體驗中心——承·風形，也將在近期開啟。 這一系列進展，向行業釋放了一個明確的訊號：空中操作機器人不再是實驗室裡的概念驗證，而是已經在真實場景中跑通的產品。 空中具身操作可能更快落地？ 縱觀具身智慧賽道，空中具身操作也許能率先突圍，比地面具身智慧更早完成規模化的商業閉環。 這一趨勢的底層支撐，源於龐大且剛性的存量運維市場缺口。 中國發電量佔全球超3

title: 蘿蔔快跑搶跑無人車右舵：香港率先全無人，倫敦直面Waymo
abstract: 蘿蔔快跑搶跑無人車右舵：香港率先全無人，倫敦直面Waymo 傑西卡 2026-07-29 13:36:38 來源： 量子位 角逐全球最難右舵市場 傑西卡 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 全球Robotaxi下一輪競爭，開始駛入右舵市場。 7月23日，香港運輸署批准 百度蘿蔔快跑 在機場島開展車上無人化測試， 車內不再設定安全員 。 這是香港首個車內全無人的自動駕駛公開道路測試，也是全球首次在右舵左行交通體系中推進全無人測試。 短短一週內，新的重要進展接踵而至。蘿蔔快跑宣佈分別攜手Uber，以及Lyft旗下歐洲出行平臺Freenow，在英國倫敦啟動公開道路測試，至此蘿蔔快跑成為目前 唯一明確進入倫敦Robotaxi測試體系的中國無人駕駛企業 。 香港和倫敦兩張“門票”，意義重大且並不相同： 前者驗證蘿蔔快跑能否把全無人能力遷移到右舵左行體系，後者則把這項能力帶入全球監管最嚴格、道路環境最複雜的一批Robotaxi市場。 倫敦還意外成為了一個特殊的交匯點。 以往常被行業拿來隔海較量的中美兩大Robotaxi力量之巔—— 蘿蔔快跑和Waymo ，將在同一座海外城市、同一套監管環境下競速，雙方首次迎來正面交鋒。 全球右舵全無人，蘿蔔快跑先跑通了 蘿蔔快跑 近期官宣，其香港北大嶼山機場島測試專案獲批開展 全無人駕駛測試 ，並在7月27日正式啟動。 這是全球右舵市場首次開展全無人自動駕駛車輛測試。 能率先突破右舵技術壁壘，並非一日之功。為拿到全無人測試許可，蘿蔔快跑走了近兩年。 公司首次步入右舵市場是在2024年底，彼時剛獲得香港運輸署發出的 當地首張自動駕駛車輛先導牌照 。 此後，其北大嶼山專案逐步完成多車同時執行、指定人員載客、路線擴展和車速提升，同時測試範圍不斷延伸。 香港運輸署在審查完測試報告並多次實地檢查後，確認其相關測試符合安全、穩定、準確和順暢等要求，且未發現異常，最終批准蘿蔔快跑的車輛撤掉車內安全員。 這條從有人到無人的推進路徑，放在自動駕駛行業很常見。Robotaxi從道路測試走到車內無人，通常都需要從車輛數量、道路範圍、執行時段、載客許可權等維度逐級放開。 真正值得關注之處在於，大多頂尖Robotaxi玩家目前以 左舵右行 體系為主。 在無人駕駛右舵市場中，儘管Waymo等頂尖無人車也在爭分奪秒佈局，但未曾有全無人測試獲批的先例，直到蘿蔔快跑第一個走完了這條鏈路。 這證明一套主要在中國內地左舵環境中成長起來的Robotaxi系統，可以跨過交通規則和駕駛習慣的差異，將感知、決策、車輛冗餘、遠端運營及安全管理共同推進至車內無人的階段。 隨後，蘿蔔快跑宣佈的又一進展，開始把這項首次突破從技術驗證推向市場檢驗。 7月28日，蘿蔔快跑宣佈分別攜手 網約車巨頭Uber和Lyft旗下Freenow ，在倫敦啟動公開道路測試，覆蓋城市和城郊複合路況。 首期測試落地倫敦布倫特行政區，監管審批完成後，預計 2027年起 能面向市民提供無人駕駛出行服務。 根據倫敦市政府今年3月公開的資訊，目前已經與當地交通機構進行前期溝通的Robotaxi，包括Wayve、百度，以及Waymo—— 蘿蔔快跑是目前這份名單中 唯一的中國Robotaxi公司 。 自此，無人駕駛的全球競爭，開始歷史性跨出以中國和美國為主的左舵市場，正式邁入覆蓋大量發達經濟體的右舵無人區。 問題也隨之而來：全球Robotaxi已經跑出數億公里全無人里程，為什麼右舵全無人直到2026年才第一次出現？ Robotaxi右舵全無人，為什麼等到了現在？ 對於自動駕駛系統來說，右舵與左舵之間可能很容易產生一個誤解，就是把右舵適配理解成 方向盤換邊、道路規則左右翻轉 。 然而現實是，在行為預測、決策規劃和運營體繫上，右舵和左舵市場其實存在明顯差異。二者在環島方向、下客區域、公交車道使用方式和路口讓行關係等方面均不相同，系統需要重新理解車輛擁有怎樣的路權。 此外，自動駕駛最難處理的場景，往往處於規則與現實駕駛習慣之間的非標準地帶。同樣是併線、禮讓和臨停，不同城市的交通參與者，可能會留下不同距離、採取不同節奏。 例如 香港 擁有雙層巴士、紅色小巴、密集計程車、狹窄道路、複雜臨停和人工交通指揮場景。 自動駕駛車輛不僅要識別這些目標，還要判斷巴士何時駛離站臺、乘客是否可能從車頭穿出，以及其他車輛會採取怎樣的繞行動作。 這已經超出簡單的畫面映象範疇，指向整套 交通語義 的遷移。所謂交通語義，既包括寫入法規的明確規則，也包括一座城市長期形成的實際駕駛習慣。 因此，

abstract: 首個鴻蒙PC開源AI統一工作臺JiuwenSwarm，辦公程式設計一站式搞定 思邈 2026-07-29 11:29:59 來源： 量子位 讓多智慧體團隊隨時隨地為你幹活 允中 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 鴻蒙PC使用者終於不用再等。 就在上週，由華為2012實驗室、華為雲、終端小藝等團隊聯合構建的 開源Al Agent平臺openjiuwen 又有新動向，其聯合華為終端平板與PC產品線、軟體部等團隊，推出了 JiuwenSwarm蜂群智慧體的鴻蒙PC版本，這也是首個面向鴻蒙PC的開源AI統一工作臺 。 桌面辦公、程式設計，不必再在多個應用間來回切換，一個工作臺裡就能派活、推進、交付。 同時openJiuwen社群還發布了人機協同的新範式 HITS（Human in the Swarm） 。 人不僅能站在團隊外智慧（HOTS，Human on the Swarm），還可以和智慧體共同組隊，支援多人、多機協同。 這也意味著，JiuwenSwarm把Coordination Engineering（協同工程）又往前推了一步：多智慧體之間的協同卷完一輪，現在開始卷人和智慧體的協同。 以鴻蒙PC為主場，它還能和飛書、小藝等場景聯動，讓使用者在不同裝置和協作環境裡持續推進任務。 不管是辦公、程式設計、還是生活娛樂，JiuwenSwarm都能幫你搞定。 辦公場景：Agent團隊幫你高效產出 人還在高鐵上，鴻蒙PC上的AI團隊已經開工 先看一個最能體現HITS的場景：緊急任務來了，人卻不在工位。 高鐵上突然接到緊急彙報任務。不用等回公司——開啟手機飛書，幾句話喚起鴻蒙PC上的JiuwenSwarm彙報材料團隊，任務立刻開始跑。 真正的變化不是“手機上也能用”，而是人還在路上，活已經在電腦上幹著了。 整個過程 人和智慧體協同推進 ：大綱不滿意就打回，碰到技術細節隨時拉一個專家智慧體進來會診，頁面不好看就中途再加一個美化智慧體，最終稿一輪輪驗收到能用為止。 人作為團隊一員，與多個智慧體協同高效辦公！ 在鴻蒙PC上，一句話生成200頁PPT 緊急彙報之外，辦公里更高頻的痛點是批量出材料。 做PPT最難的不是寫，是動筆之前：主題怎麼拆、材料上哪找、結構怎麼搭。 彙報材料一多、時間一緊，一個人很難快速搞定。 在鴻蒙PC上輸入主題、受眾和風格要求，JiuwenSwarm選擇 叢集模式 ，由系統自動組建一支多智慧體團隊，幾個成員隨即分頭開工：有的去調研，有的梳理結構，有的補內容，有的負責整合最終結果。 原本序列的“查資料—搭大綱—補頁面”，被拆成一條可以多智慧體同步推進的任務鏈。 整個過程，20分鐘內就能搞定200頁高質量PPT！ 程式設計場景：靈感來了，隨時幫你實現 前兩個案例是高效辦公，這個場景展示的是創作與程式設計：一個臨時冒出的念頭，能不能變成能跑的應用？ 想玩的遊戲商店裡沒有？那就自己造一個 第一個案例是有使用者想重溫小時候的街機坦克大戰，翻遍軟體商店沒找到合適版本，於是在鴻蒙PC上開啟JiuwenSwarm，使用 Code下的叢集模式 ，讓系統組一支小型開發團隊—— 一個成員設計玩法和介面，一個前端開發，一個後端開發，一個做測試驗證，Leader統籌節奏。 前端和後端開發分別在 不同分支獨立並行開發 ，完成後再統一合入主幹。 幾輪協作之後，坦克大戰真的在鴻蒙PC上跑了起來，開發過程中，想到新點子， 還能@某個成員，給他加需求 。 第二個案例更日常，使用者正在健身，想給自己做一個簡單、乾淨、夠用的熱量記錄工具。 開啟鴻蒙PC上的JiuwenSwarm，切換Code模式，描述需求後，系統 自主規劃任務、完成ArkTS程式碼開發 ，經過編譯後，生成一個可在鴻蒙PC上安裝執行的熱量記錄應用。 靈感稍縱即逝，難的是做出來——搭架構、寫程式碼、測試驗證….JiuwenSwarm直接都幫你搞定。 生活娛樂：工作之外，與AI組隊遊戲 HITS的作用不止於協同辦公：下了班，人還能和智慧體組隊打遊戲。 工作之外，它也能拉你開一局小遊戲 先看一局五子棋小遊戲：使用JiuwenSwarm在鴻蒙PC上組建一支五子棋遊戲團隊，由智慧體擔任主持人，邀請兩位人類玩家入場。 兩人都準備好，輸入“開始遊戲”，對局正式啟動。 過程中主持人同步棋盤、維護規則、提醒玩家落子，就像是有人在現場帶著玩，不知道下一步棋落在哪兒？智慧體還能給你推薦位置。 場景很輕鬆，但也說明了一件事：智慧體不只會埋頭幹活，還能站出來當組織者，把一件需要多人配合的事從頭到尾張羅明白。 這一次，你

title: 周鴻禕釋出奈米Work：新一代企業智慧體工作平臺，為企業而生
abstract: 周鴻禕釋出奈米Work：新一代企業智慧體工作平臺，為企業而生 量子位的朋友們 2026-07-29 09:53:15 來源： 量子位 7月28日，360集團創始人周鴻禕正式釋出新一代企業智慧體工作平臺“奈米Work”。奈米Work為企業AI化而生，面向企業老闆、創業者及一人公司（OPC）和企業員工，打造超級組織。釋出會現場，周鴻禕提出一個鮮明的觀點：企業搞AI，老闆要先用。他同時宣佈為首批使用者每人提供1億Token試用額度，通過專業實訓和陪跑服務，率先幫助1000家小企業完成AI落地和經營提效。 周鴻禕透露，釋出產品前，360先把自己作為“試驗場”，將OpenClaw等各類智慧體投入公司1000多個真實業務場景，收集56000多條使用者反饋意見，在5個月內最佳化迭代166個版本後，最終推出奈米Work。他表示，奈米Work不是對某一款智慧體的簡單封裝，而是希望將複雜技術能力隱藏起來，將先進能力轉化為使用者可直接使用的生產力，同時融入原生安全能力。 據瞭解，智慧體落地企業過程中面臨挑戰：複雜任務可能帶來不可預估的Token消耗，普通使用者需要面對環境配置、模型選擇、工具連線等門檻，而企業更加關注許可權邊界、任務穩定性以及資料安全。周鴻禕表示，智慧體真正進入工作場景，需要同時解決成本、門檻、許可權、穩定性、安全性和持續進化等問題。 針對這些挑戰，奈米Work構建了多智慧體引擎、多模型底座、雲端辦公室、多工作模式和多專家五大能力體系。使用者無需研究模型、智慧體框架和工具，只需提出目標，平臺即可根據任務需求組織不同AI專家協同工作，並匹配合適的模型和執行方式。企業老闆可以藉助奈米Work輔助經營分析、業務增長和進度管理；創業者及一人公司可以完成機會發現、產品驗證、內容生產和營銷獲客；企業員工則可以利用AI提升資料研究、方案策劃、內容製作和專案交付效率，成為職場精英。 企業智慧體要進入真實工作場景，首先必須解決安全問題。周鴻禕表示：“大模型出錯，是說錯話；智慧體出錯，是幹錯事。”針對智慧體執行任務帶來的新安全挑戰，360將“原生安全、出廠內建”作為奈米Work設計原則，通過雲端隔離、許可權控制、資料保護等安全機制，降低企業使用AI過程中的風險，讓企業敢於把真實工作交給AI。 釋出會現場，新疆喀什網紅早餐店”香香手”的老闆阿布拉江來到現場，分享了藉助奈米Work做品牌營銷、做店鋪設計、做法務諮詢推動店鋪擴張的經驗。從一家早餐店發展到6家門店，阿布拉江的實踐展現了AI正在進入更多普通創業者的真實經營場景。 周鴻禕認為，AI正在進入“模型與智慧體雙線進化”的階段，“模型決定AI有多聰明，智慧體決定AI能不能真正幹活”。未來企業競爭不僅取決於模型能力，更取決於能否將模型、知識、工具和業務流程結合起來，形成穩定的任務交付能力。 同時，360啟動奈米Work城市合夥人招募，進一步完善本地化服務和落地支援，推動奈米Work進入更多門店、園區和企業真實業務場景，加速AI普惠應用。 更多關於奈米Work產品資訊，請訪問官方網站： work.n.cn 本文由360提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 360 量子位的朋友們 OceanBase回應融資報道：全力投入AI資料創新，與資本市場保持開放溝通 2026-07-29 空中具身操作：讓蜘蛛俠們安全落地 2026-07-29 九章雲極Alaya Token完成Kimi K3適配 全球首個開源3T級模型入駐Token工廠 2026-07-29 Kimi K3、Unlimited OCR包攬全球前二，中國開源模型持續刷屏海外 2026-07-28 掃碼分享至朋友圈 相關閱讀 OpenClaw創始人回信確認360獨家發現漏洞 推進智慧體應用的實戰化防禦。 量子位 2026-03-23 360 OpenClaw 360重磅釋出企業級智慧體平臺，啟動“千行”計劃加速產業智變 實現智慧體“能用、好用、放心用” 鷺羽 2025-10-28 360 Agent 360集團梁志輝：企業不能指望員工都變成AI發燒友｜MEET2024 大模型商業應用，360看好三大場景 夢晨 2023-12-18 360 MEET2024智慧未來大會 MEET智慧未來大會 周鴻禕：網路安全不是一門“賣貨”的生意 還是熟悉的紅色Polo衫 夢晨 2021-08-05 360 周鴻禕 網路安全 駭客 周鴻禕：大模型不是作業系統，將成為數字化系統標配 360智腦行業解決方案將率

abstract: 九章雲極Alaya Token完成Kimi K3適配 全球首個開源3T級模型入駐Token工廠 量子位的朋友們 2026-07-29 09:45:36 來源： 量子位 近日，九章雲極DataCanvas旗下專業Token規模化交付平臺Alaya Token正式完成對Kimi K3模型的深度適配與生產級上線。此舉標誌著九章雲極“AI工廠”戰略在模型生態建設上再落關鍵一子，繼智譜GLM-5.2、DeepSeek-V4 Flash之後，其Token工廠的“多模型矩陣”已覆蓋當前國內頭部開源模型梯隊。 據悉，Kimi K3 是全球首個開源的 3 萬億參數級大模型。它採用自研的 KDA 混合線性注意力機制（Kimi Delta Attention）與注意力殘差架構，以 2.8 萬億參數的 MoE 設計原生支援視覺理解，上下文視窗達 100 萬 token。在程式設計、Agent 與複雜推理等基準上，K3 全面進入開源模型第一梯隊——Frontend Code Arena 以 1679 分位列全球第一，超過 Claude Fable 5；據第三方評測，SWE-bench Verified 達 76.8%。 作為AI工廠戰略的核心落地載體，Alaya Token依託智算叢集資源底座，貫通模型研發、智慧封裝到規模化交付全鏈路，為開發者與企業提供標準化、可計量、按需付費的一站式Token算力服務。Alaya Token的核心價值在於構建了“聚合而不鎖定”的模型服務生態。企業無需為不同模型分別採購算力套餐，一套金鑰即可在多個模型間自由切換。在本次Kimi K3的適配中，九章雲極工程團隊針對其長上下文特性完成了底層運算元最佳化與KV Cache動態排程，確保長程任務推理的穩定吞吐。 目前，Alaya Token已深度服務於金融風控、工業質檢、程式碼生成等ToB高價值場景，持續推動AI能力從技術驗證走向規模交付。 立即體驗：https://codingplan.alayanew.com/ 本文由九章雲極提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 九章雲極 量子位的朋友們 OceanBase回應融資報道：全力投入AI資料創新，與資本市場保持開放溝通 2026-07-29 空中具身操作：讓蜘蛛俠們安全落地 2026-07-29 周鴻禕釋出奈米Work：新一代企業智慧體工作平臺，為企業而生 2026-07-29 Kimi K3、Unlimited OCR包攬全球前二，中國開源模型持續刷屏海外 2026-07-28 掃碼分享至朋友圈 相關閱讀 剛剛，北京建了一座AI工廠：目標10萬P算力，日產10萬億Token！ 計劃1000倍綜合降本 十三 2026-06-17 token Token工廠 九章雲極 算力 訓練工廠

title: 豆包搜尋，走出了豆包
abstract: 豆包搜尋，走出了豆包 十三 2026-07-28 18:12:52 來源： 量子位 把搜尋能力開放給Agent了 金磊 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 豆包 APP裡的 搜尋 能力，現在要走出豆包了—— 一頭扎進面向企業和開發者的Agent，目標是想讓Agent獲取資訊的這件事情，變得更加靠譜。 我們先用最近大熱的話題 菲爾茲獎 ，來看下走出來的 豆包搜尋 ，實力到底幾何。 這類題目看上去不算複雜，真要做好，卻得同時滿足幾個條件。 資訊得足夠新，獲獎名單和研究貢獻不能出錯；來源也得足夠可靠，官方公告、媒體報道和人物資料最好能夠相互印證。 這次的結果裡，有一個地方需要先講清楚。 這次豆包搜尋返回了3條與問題直接相關的資料，分別來自政府官網轉載、科技日報，以及西蒙斯基金會的相關內容。 重點不只在於找到了哪些頁面。每條結果還同時帶回了信源名稱、權威分級、釋出時間、圍繞當前問題生成的正文摘要，以及能夠直接引用的原文Markdown節選。 從用途來看，第一條資料適合核對獲獎名單和官方獲獎理由；第二條補充了兩位中國數學家的研究方向與成果；第三條則提供了國際組織和專業機構對本屆獲獎者的評價。 若繼續交給Agent處理，它可以先利用權威分級和釋出時間判斷資料是否可靠、是否足夠新，再直接從正文摘要和原文節選中提取獲獎名單、研究貢獻和媒體評價。 這也是豆包搜尋和只返回網頁入口的搜尋有所不同的地方。Agent拿到的不只是一串連結，還包括判斷資料能不能用所需的關鍵欄位。 大模型很擅長理解、歸納和推理，但它天然有知識更新時間的邊界。只要問題碰到新事件、新版本和新價格，單靠模型腦子裡的“存量知識”就不夠用了。 這時候，如果搜尋只給出網頁入口，Agent還要繼續開啟頁面、理解正文、抽取資訊。豆包搜尋想省下的，正是中間這段反覆讀取和處理網頁的過程。 所以，到了Agent階段，搜尋能力的關鍵已經不只是能不能找到網頁，還要看返回的資訊能否直接進入下一步任務。 簡單理解，火山引擎是把豆包APP背後的搜尋能力單獨拆出來，再通過API、MCP、Skill等方式，接進更多模型和Agent裡。 據瞭解，目前豆包搜尋已經正式面向企業和開發者開放，每月會 贈送500次免費搜尋額度 ，同時支援按量後付費和訂閱月卡。 為了瞭解豆包搜尋的更多能力，一波實測，走起~ Agent都會上網，開始拼“怎麼搜”和“搜什麼” 在正式開始之前，先簡單交代一下這次的實測環境。 我們在Mac本地搭建了OpenClaw，並接入Doubao-Seed-Evolving作為Agent模型。搜尋這一側，則單獨安裝了火山引擎提供的byted-web-search Skill。 安裝只需要一條命令： npx skills add https: //skills.volces.com/skills/bytedance/agentkit-samples -s byted-web-search —agent openclaw 隨後，再到 火山引擎豆包搜尋 的控制台建立API Key，完成介面配置。 接下來的三個Case都在 OpenClaw Dashboard 裡完成。我們會在Prompt中明確指定呼叫byted-web-search，並在截圖中同時保留使用者輸入和搜尋結果。 為了方便觀察，豆包搜尋每次只展示3條代表性資料。除了標題和來源，結果裡還會帶回權威分級、釋出時間、正文摘要和原文Markdown節選。 至於Agent後續會採用哪些資料、每條資料分別能支撐什麼結論，我們放在文字中簡要說明。 第一個Case ，正好撞上了一條剛剛發生的新訊息。 就在昨天深夜，Kimi K3迎來正式開源。新訊息出來得足夠近，也很適合測試豆包搜尋對最新事件的反應速度，以及它能否迅速定位到官方資訊。 從結果來看，豆包搜尋返回了3條與Kimi K3開放權重直接相關的資料，而且都帶有明確的釋出時間。 第一條來自新浪財經旗下的國是直通車，釋出時間為7月28日10時54分，摘要中提取出了模型權重、技術報告，以及MoonEP、FlashKDA、AgentEnv等訓練基礎設施。 第二條來自IT之家，釋出時間為7月27日23時14分，進一步補充了模型參數、GitHub和Hugging Face入口、部署要求及API價格。 第三條釋出於7月28日6時32分，重點解釋了Kimi K3 License及這次開放的邊界——公開的重點是模型權重，並不等於完整訓練程式碼同步開源。 若繼續交給Agent加工，第一條適合確認權重

title: Kimi K3、Unlimited OCR包攬全球前二，中國開源模型持續刷屏海外
abstract: Kimi K3、Unlimited OCR包攬全球前二，中國開源模型持續刷屏海外 量子位的朋友們 2026-07-28 16:17:05 來源： 量子位 中國AI開源模型持續引發全球開發者關注，創新成果正在集中湧現。 7月27日晚，月之暗面正式開源 Kimi K3 完整模型權重，隨即登上國際開源AI模型社群Hugging Face總趨勢榜第一，緊隨其後的則是多日位列榜首的百度開源模型 Unlimited OCR，兩者包攬了Hugging Face榜單前二，堪稱中國模型“開源雙子星”。 模型登頂本身並不稀缺，但Kimi K3 和 Unlimited OCR 在極短時間內製造了兩個現象級爆款： Kimi K3 釋出後，幾十分鐘內迅速登頂 Hugging Face 趨勢榜，重新整理平臺的增長紀錄。Unlimited OCR 更為罕見，5天內GitHub Star突破 1 萬，首發即登頂 GitHub Daily Trending 總榜和Python 榜，HuggingFace 全球模型總趨勢榜和多模態模型趨勢榜，實現 GitHub、HuggingFace 四榜第一； 在釋出一個月後， Unlimited OCR 熱度再次攀升，獲圖靈獎得主、AI科學家楊立昆轉發，一舉重回Hugging Face 全球模型總趨勢榜第一 。截至目前，Unlimited OCR 在GitHub Star 已突破 1.97萬，HuggingFace 下載量達到 265 萬。 Unlimited OCR受到開發者持續關注，並非只是效能領先，更重要的是推動了長檔案解析技術向前邁出關鍵一步。過去，OCR 模型面對書籍、論文、報告等長檔案時，通常需要採用“逐頁解析+結果拼接”的工程方案，隨著輸出內容不斷增長，解碼階段的 KV Cache 持續膨脹，推理速度和視訊記憶體成本也隨之增加。 針對這一行業痛點，百度提出 Reference Sliding Window Attention （R-SWA）機制 ，借鑑人類閱讀和抄錄長檔案時的工作方式——始終保持對原始檔案內容的關注，同時僅保留最近一段生成內容作為“工作記憶”，而不是無限累積全部歷史資訊。基於這一設計，模型能夠在一次前向推理中連續完成數十頁檔案解析，實現從第一頁到最後一頁的連貫輸出，同時將解碼階段的 KV Cache 控制在恆定規模，使計算成本和視訊記憶體佔用不隨輸出長度持續增長。 業內人士表示，這一突破不僅在於讓 OCR 解析更快、更準，更重要的是為大模型長程推理和記憶管理提供了新的思路。相較於依賴不斷擴展上下文視窗提升能力，這一創新探索了以更高效的注意力機制實現長期任務處理的新路徑。 也正因為解決了開發者長期面臨的實際問題，Unlimited OCR的熱度並未隨著時間推移而消退，而是在海外開發者社群持續爆火，一個月後重新回到Hugging Face全球模型趨勢榜第一。 在開源社群，專案釋出初期登上趨勢榜並不罕見，但在熱度回落後，僅憑開發者持續使用與口碑傳播再次上榜的案例並不多見。此前，DeepSeek-R1 曾在模型釋出、API 開放等多個節點多次進入趨勢榜；而 Unlimited OCR 僅憑全球開發者持續下載、部署、使用和推薦，時隔一個月再次登頂 Hugging Face 全球模型總趨勢榜。這表明，Unlimited OCR 的影響力已從釋出熱度延伸至持續的開發者採用和社群傳播，也折射出中國 AI 開源正從“釋出即關注”邁向“持續被採用”，國際影響力進一步沉澱為全球開發者生態影響力。 據悉，百度堅持和貫徹開源理念由來已久。不止模型，此前更將AI基礎設施底座如PaddlePaddle深度學習框架、Apollo自動駕駛平臺等開源，一些成熟通用工程專案像ECharts、bRPC、Doris、HugeGraph等捐給國際開源基金會Apache，積極融入全球開源體系。 近年來，中國人工智慧企業圍繞推理、多模態、長文本、檔案智慧等關鍵方向持續實現原創突破，逐步形成多點開花、協同創新的發展格局。從DeepSeek、Kimi，再到百度Unlimited OCR，中國AI輸出的不僅是具有國際競爭力的模型，更是不斷貢獻原創技術、開源生態和創新範式。中國人工智慧正從參與全球競爭邁向貢獻全球創新，為培育發展新質生產力以及全球人工智慧技術進步注入更多中國智慧和中國方案。 Unlimited OCR開源地址： GitHub：https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR HuggingFace

title: 當AI學會“模擬思維”，教師才能迴歸育人本質
abstract: 當AI學會“模擬思維”，教師才能迴歸育人本質 量子位的朋友們 2026-07-28 15:32:47 來源： 量子位 從“工具效率”到“認知理解”，教育AI進入深水區 2026年，教育部等五部門印發《“人工智慧+教育”行動計劃》，檔案明確要求分層提升教師AI數字素養，全面構建人機協同的新型課堂模式。政策方向已然明朗，但落地層面的討論仍在發酵。7月23日，復旦大學副校長周磊在接受人民網專訪時表示：“智慧化轉型浪潮下，教學創新比任何時候都更關乎教育本質。”他同時指出，一線教師首要的能力迭代，是從“AI工具使用者”轉向“智慧教學設計者”。 這句話精準點出當眾多學校共同面臨的深層焦慮——教育AI應用並不稀缺，但多數浮於表面，難以真正服務因材施教，教師轉型缺少完整支撐體系。 當前AI賦能教育存在三大結構性難題： 第一，師資結構性缺口難以消解。 縣域、鄉村學校骨幹教師稀缺，大班額下教師無力兼顧後進生補差與優等生拔高，大量時間消耗在學情統計、習題整理等標準化工作，無暇開展價值引領、情感浸潤等AI不可替代的育人工作； 第二，AI應用淺層化難以突破。 市面上碎片化智慧產品只能完成內容推送，無法模擬學生真實思維短板，教師缺少完整理論框架支撐個性化教學設計，很難轉型為課堂“總導演”與學習設計師； 第三，教師AI轉型缺少配套體系。 各校零散採購工具、自主摸索融合路徑，試錯成本高昂，同時學生心智資料安全、AI學術倫理缺少統一規範，學校不敢大規模推廣智慧教學。 換言之，行業需要的不再是單點工具，而是從普惠、認知到治理的體系化能力。近期的一些行業實踐，提供了可供觀察的樣本。 一線普惠實踐：“一生一案”補齊師資短板，迴歸價值育人核心 推進教育均衡、縮小城鄉校際差距，是《“人工智慧+教育”行動計劃》核心任務之一。偏遠縣域學校普遍存在師資薄弱問題，城市教師則深陷機械性教學事務，分層教學長期難以落地。天立啟鳴打造的“天立學科大腦・一生一案”個性化學習方案，從全球40個國家267份申報案例中脫穎而出，成功入選聯合國ITU 2026 AI for Good全球創新案例，成為落實聯合國SDG4優質教育目標的中國基層實踐樣本。 該方案底層邏輯為“AI做助教、教師為主導”，絕不以技術替代教師。系統承接全流程算力密集型工作：學情精準診斷、分層教學資源匹配、個性化習題智慧適配、班級學習資料彙總復盤，填補師資總量不足、分佈不均帶來的結構性空白。 據校方統計，方案在雲南彝良國家重點幫扶縣落地一年後，當地學校本科上線率提升至88.5%，班級後20%後進生的進步幅度明顯超過前20%。截至目前，這套體系已在全國150餘所中小學常態化落地，累計服務30萬餘名師生，輕量化部署適配公辦、民辦、城鄉各類學校，無需大規模硬體改造，真正為基礎薄弱學生提供普惠化分層學習支援，也讓教師從重複勞動中抽身，聚焦情感引導與價值塑造。 認知世界模型破解“偽個性化推薦”，築牢資料安全倫理底線 普惠之後是更深的追問：AI能否真正理解學習者？，而不只是高效地分發內容？ 不少教師反饋：即便系統推送海量習題，學生成績提升依舊緩慢。因為當前絕大多數教育AI，本質上還是基於“統計關聯”的內容推薦引擎。傳統教育AI僅依託答題結果做統計匹配，無法區分學生錯題根源是概念混淆、邏輯斷層還是審題疏漏。 針對這一瓶頸，天立啟鳴聯合北京航空航天大學國際創新研究院、AIII人工智慧國際研究院等機構，在2026世界人工智慧大會期間釋出《世界模型驅動的教育AGI白皮書》，率先將認知世界模型（CWM）引入基礎教育場景。 通俗地說，未來的教育AI不再是一個龐大的“題庫檢索器”，而是一個“學生大腦的模擬器”：通過LAM（學習評估建模）閉環，觀測學生的做題行為，在虛擬空間裡“建模”出學生的認知狀態，推導思維盲區，進而規劃出適配的學習路徑。 同時，白皮書提出“認知主權”倫理框架，將學生心智推斷資料納入分級保護範疇，從技術底層劃定學生學習資料安全邊界，回應了學校側對學生資料安全的核心關切，也為教師開展高階人機協同教學設計提供方法論支撐，助力教師完成從簡單操作工具到“智慧教學設計者”的轉型。 科研級智慧體賽事驗證能力，支撐高階素養教學設計 AI要勝任更複雜的教學協同，底層能力與行業規範同樣關鍵。在第四屆世界科學智慧大賽中，天立啟鳴團隊從全球32個國家和地區、近1.8萬名選手中突圍並獲得三等獎；其智慧體實踐同時入選中國資訊通訊研究院《2026智慧經濟新形態：智慧體創新實踐案例彙編》，是其中為數不多來自教育領域的案例。 從科研賽事到入選

title: 關於 Agent 的幾個判斷
abstract: See all posts Published on 2026-07-28 關於 Agent 的幾個判斷 作者： 寶玉 @cellier_ 昨天發了一條帖子，談了他對 Agent 的三個判斷： 一是，通用 Agent 會吃掉垂直 Agent。Codex、Claude Cowork、WorkBuddy 這些通用型選手，配合 Skill 和 MCP，就能搞定大部分專業任務。很多 AI-native 應用創業，本身就是個偽命題。 二是，更開放的會吃掉更封閉的。模型能力趨同之後，會變成可路由的基礎設施。Agent 應該讓使用者自由選擇模型，甚至支援本地部署和自由遷移。 三是，更下沉的會吃掉更傲慢的。Codex、Claude、DeepSeek 背後的團隊都以 AGI 為目標，不太願意做髒活累活，這就給了草根團隊做精細化運營的機會視窗。 我覺得這是個很好的話題，也說說我的幾個判斷。 1. 少數通用 Agent 通吃 不只是通用 Agent 會吃掉垂直 Agent，通用 Agent 這個賽道本身，也會是少數贏家通吃。 小的通用 Agent 同樣沒有生存空間。 2. 基於 Agent 的外掛系統至關重要 開放和封閉的差別，不在於是不是開源，也不在於能不能自由切換模型，而在於它的外掛生態。 最受歡迎的 Claude Code 和 Codex，預設使用的都是自家模型，但這並沒有造成多大影響，何況它們也都支援通過 API 使用其他模型。 現在 Agent 之所以能火起來，一個重要原因就是豐富的外掛生態。Skill 加 MCP，可以幫助 Agent 完成各種不同的任務。 3. 前期的 Agent 更多是在教育使用者 “下沉”和“傲慢”都是很主觀的說法。 WorkBuddy 那樣不見得就叫下沉，Codex 也不見得傲慢。當然，說 Anthropic 傲慢，可能沒什麼爭議。但只要模型足夠強，大家捏著鼻子也就認了。 Agent 這種產品，使用者沒有那麼多忠誠度。前期的產品，本質上都是在教育使用者。 就像“小龍蝦”，雖然現在已經沒人提了，但它確實起到了普及 Agent 的作用。將來寫 AGI 發展史，也算留下過一筆。 WorkBuddy 現在火爆，也是在教育使用者，讓很多不知道或者用不了 Codex 和 Claude Code 的人，也能用上 Agent。 想當年 Claude Code 多火爆，後來 Codex 推出 GUI 版，也很快搶走了不少使用者。 4. 模型是護城河 Agent 的產品體驗其實也沒有多深的護城河，最後都會趨同。模型能力和成本，終究還是會讓產品拉開差距。 Skills 和 MCP 絕大部分都不具備獨佔性。在一個 Agent 平臺能用，換個平臺通常也能繼續用。 使用者使用 Agent 時，最大的體驗差異來自模型本身的智慧程度。 當你用過聰明的模型，就不會想再回到不那麼聰明的模型。很多人願意接受當下的產品，只是因為沒有機會用到更好的。一旦有機會用上更聰明、更便宜的模型，他們會毫不猶豫地切換，絲毫不會有忠誠度。 Cursor 的 Agent 體驗也很好，什麼模型都能用。但熱度最高的依然是 Codex 和 Claude Code，因為它們有訂閱服務，價效比更高。 5. 個人開發者和小團隊沒必要拼 Agent 小團隊做通用 Agent、垂直 Agent，已經沒什麼機會了。但是，基於 Agent 做外掛，仍然有很多機會。 很多傳統軟體並不是為 Agent 設計的，這裡面還有一個時間視窗。 Skills 已經氾濫了，單純做一個 Skill 沒什麼門檻。讓 Skill 作為入口，後面再接入服務，還是有機會的，這也是提供差異化的地方。 6. 普通使用者越早用、越多用 Agent，越受益 AI Agent 不會替代你，但它可以替你完成很多電腦上的重複工作。越早用起來，就越早享受它帶來的效率提升。 多花一點錢，用更聰明的模型，可以節約你的時間，也能提升使用體驗。把錢花在聰明的模型上是值得的，當然也沒必要超出自己的承受能力。 你要相信 Agent 能幫你提升效率，它就一定能幫到你。信則靈。 除非是為了測試，否則沒必要安裝很多 Skills，尤其不要安裝全域性 Skills。但要學會讓 Agent 幫你寫 Skills，並持續迭代自己的 Skills。 管理能力，尤其是工程管理能力，會越來越重要。因為普通人也需要管理 Agent，而管理 Agent 和管理專案，本來就有很多相似之處。 有條件的話，換一臺 Mac 電腦。它是 Agent 的最佳搭檔。 See all posts

title: [AINews] Fearing RSI: OpenAI, Anthropic, GDM, Meta, Thinky cosign letter to "Pace" AI development, as HuggingFace details Machine-Speed Offensive Cyberattack
abstract: 3 years ago, Elon Musk and Yoshua Bengio cosigned the Future of Life’s letter arguing for a 6 month pause in AI , which most frontier AI leaders gleefully ignored. Today, the pausers have the last laugh. Yesterday, we said that unless you “make law, make chips, or make models”, you can probably ignore the current debate about open weights models (those of you who shouted us out, thank you!) Today, we have something we CANNOT ignore: over 1,000 frontier lab employees, from substantively all frontier labs except X.ai, have cosigned a different statement: “AI could help create a dramatically better future, but that outcome is not guaranteed. The world’s leading AI companies believe they could be close to automating AI research . It is hard to predict exactly how much this will accelerate AI progress, but there is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems . To realize AI’s potential, industry, government, and society at large may need the option to buy time to address emerging risks, develop security measures, and strengthen oversight. But each company—and country—is under intense competitive pressure not to unilaterally slow that acceleration. And today, the world lacks the technical and governance tools to deliberately pace frontier-wide progress. Building on work already underway to monitor frontier model releases: We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.” - 1,171 employees of frontier AI companies While it is framed as an action taken in “personal capacity and do not necessarily represent any company’s views”, but when Dario is cosigning, Sam is on podcasts agreeing , and the official @OpenAI account is tweeting this letter , let’s just say the letter is a little more official than Denny’s signing the Nvidia letter for a quick laugh. title: Codex from 0 to 10M Users: Building ChatGPT Work — Akshay Nathan, OpenAI
abstract: There are roughly 100x more people who use code than who can write code. 1 As code that “just works” becomes easier to generate, this group may be the biggest prize of all — if you can get the agentic interface right. A key trend we have been tracking over at AINews is the absolute explosion in Codex usage this year , with MAU now up >10x from Jan 2026 . Less than two weeks after their July 9th launch , OpenAI said ChatGPT Work and Codex had reached 10M million users combined (as we cover in the pod, Codex now powers ChatGPT Work, so all ChatGPT Work users are now users of the Codex harness, even if they aren’t traditional engineers) — showing the early innings of what happens when you graduate from coding agents to knowledge work agents: We’ve been calling out how coding agents are “breaking containment” to do everything else this year to power every other part of knowledge work - and it started with the org chart, with a major reorg last month that amounted to two of Codex’s most prominent leaders, Greg and Tibo, taking responsibility over product and ChatGPT specifically, completing a “Superapp” consolidation cycle first discussed in March . With these updates Codex is no longer just a coding tool. In June, OpenAI said knowledge workers already accounting for roughly 20% of Codex’s user base and growing more than 3x as quickly as developers. ChatGPT Work now enables users to work across every primitive with agents. title: Everyone is unique: Towards Behaviorally Heterogeneous Negotiation Dialogue Systems for Debt Collection
abstract: Debt collection is a critical negotiation task in the financial industry, with strong practical relevance and exceptional academic value as a behaviorally rich, high-stakes testbed for human-centered dialogue systems. While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in dialogue and negotiation, effectively evaluating their performance in this complex scenarios remains a major challenge: existing benchmarks uniformly assume users to be static, rational agents with fixed preferences, failing to capture the rich behavioral heterogeneity inherent in real-world debt collection. To bridge this gap, we propose DebtBench, the first public persona-enriched debt collection benchmark, that highlights behavioral heterogeneity in negotiation. Moreover, we develop DebtGPT, a debt collection agent trained to jointly optimize financial recovery and interaction experience. Our experimental results, using 16 state-of-the-art LLMs, find that most existing models struggle in this complex but realistic scenarios, whereas DebtGPT outperforms all open-source baselines and achieves performance on par with GPT-4o. The code and data are available at https://github.com/YYuHhhh/DebtNegotiation.

title: Inspect India Evals: An Open Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Large Language Models in the Indian Linguistic and Cultural Context
abstract: India is a vast nation of over 1.4 billion people, varied by hundreds of diverse and locally specific traditions and cultures and 22 officially recognized languages. Large language models (LLMs) are now being deployed on a massive scale throughout the mainland as well as in remote villages. However, the common benchmarks - MMLU, BIG-Bench, and TruthfulQA are almost exclusively English- and Western-centric. They do not identify those safety, fairness, and accuracy failures unique to the Indian context. That is the gap Inspect India Evals seeks to fill. It is an open-source framework built on top of UK AISI's Inspect AI platform. It has six benchmarks: Multilingual MMLU across sixteen Indian languages, BharatBBQ (our adaptation of BBQ for Indian social bias), a safety evaluation for Digital Public Infrastructure, a multilingual safety test using harmful prompts in Indian languages, a multi-turn jailbreak resistance test, and an Indian cultural knowledge benchmark scored using LLM-as-judge rubrics. In this study, we tested five open-weight models ranging from 8B to 32B parameters. Sarvam-M 24B and Gemma 2 27B came out on top, both scoring 80% on the composite India Fairness Index, with Sarvam-M even beating larger 32B models on Indian cultural knowledge and DPI safety compliance. All models scored 100% refusal on Multilingual Safety, whereas DPI safety varied from 20% to 100%. The framework is public. It's built to work with the UK AISI registry. Anyone can reproduce or extend this work.

title: Sense it with your eyes: Sensation Generation and Understanding for Advertisements
abstract: Sensory advertising evokes human senses through visual cues, enabling audiences to mentally simulate experiences and increasing persuasive impact. Despite the recent increase in using AI in generating and understanding creative and persuasive content, how advertisements visually evoke sensations remains largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce the first study of understanding, evaluating, and generating sensory ads. We introduce the Sensory Ad dataset, and define sensation classification tasks (SenseClass) to benchmark LLMs and MLLMs. We further propose SenseScore, an automated evaluation metric for sensation evocation achieving strong agreement with human judgments. Finally, we introduce the Sensory Ad Generation (SenseGen) task and propose SAGA, a multi-agent framework that improves message image alignment, sensory evocation, and persuasion. Our work establishes a foundation for sensory-aware visual persuasion.

title: The Disruptive Impact of Large Language Models on Capture the Flag Competitions and the Path Toward Fair Play
abstract: Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions are among cybersecurity's most effective training grounds, developing practical skill across cryptography, web exploitation, and binary exploitation. Large language models (LLMs) can now solve a growing share of challenges with minimal human input, raising urgent questions about fairness, the validity of rankings, and whether participation still delivers the learning that justifies the effort. This paper reports a mixed-methods study of LLM impact on modern CTFs, combining a synthesis of published benchmarks, including a recent government evaluation, case studies of live competition across three challenge categories, structured observation of the public channels where the community debates AI use, and semi-structured interviews with experienced players and organisers. We map the current human-machine capability boundary by category, showing that easy and intermediate challenges in cryptography, web, and binary exploitation are now reliably automated while narrower sub-categories continue to resist. We find that community disagreement about whether AI should be permitted is downstream of an undeclared prior question: what a competition is for. Against this backdrop we contribute a four-component safeguard framework, combining tiered competition divisions, LLM-resistant challenge design, telemetry used investigatively, and a draft community code of conduct, together with a decision tool that ties the combination of safeguards to a competition's declared purpose. The argument reaches beyond CTFs to any setting in cybersecurity where a demonstrated result is taken as evidence of an underlying ability.

title: Agentic AI in medicine: architectures, applications, evaluation, and challenges for clinical translation
abstract: Large language models and multimodal foundation models are enabling medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems to move beyond isolated prediction and undertake multistep clinical tasks that require planning, tool use, memory, iterative correction, and coordination among specialized agents. However, the scope of agentic AI in medicine remains unsettled, and current evaluation practices are not yet aligned with the requirements of clinical use. We conducted a scoping review with systematic evidence mapping across five electronic sources, screened 1,649 exportable records, and provisionally included 557 unique studies that met predefined criteria for goal-directed task execution, tool use, interaction with external resources, feedback-based refinement, or multi-agent collaboration. The included studies describe single agents that use external tools, workflows supported by retrieval and external knowledge, multimodal agents, and multi-agent systems applied to medical question answering, image interpretation, electronic health record analysis, drug safety, and clinical trial prediction. The evidence base remains dominated by public benchmarks, simulated settings, retrospective datasets, and small-scale expert evaluation. Process reliability, evidence traceability, uncertainty, safety, workflow impact, and external validity are evaluated less consistently. Clinical translation will depend on clearer definitions, reproducible evaluation, auditable oversight, interoperable system design, and prospective validation in real-world clinical workflows.

title: Cardiologent: Multi-Agent Clinical Decision Support for Patient-Level Arrhythmia Assessment, Urgency, and Management
abstract: The same episode of atrial fibrillation is a minor finding in a healthy adult and grounds for anticoagulation in an elderly patient with hypertension: identical signal, opposite decision. Naming the rhythm is only the start; what determines a patient's outcome is the judgement that follows -- what the arrhythmia is across the whole record, what it means for this patient, and what should be done about it. Recent work pairing large language models with the ECG stops short of this, reading one recording without assembling a patient-level finding; and agentic systems built around it either receive the arrhythmia a device has already detected or target a different diagnostic task, stopping before the decision this task requires. We formulate patient-level arrhythmia decision support as a task and present Cardiologent, a multi-agent system that spans it from detection to decision. An agent for each signal -- a single ECG lead and the photoplethysmogram a wearable acquires -- grounds its window reading in measured features rather than a bare label; the readings are assembled into the patient's rhythm profile and, with the patient's own data, reasoned against clinical guidelines retrieved for the case, with a critic checking each conclusion against the guideline it cites. We evaluate the clinical decision rather than the report, across integrated diagnosis, clinical significance, and urgency and management. Cardiologent scores highest on every axis, first on every patient-level task under both cardiologists and an at-scale LLM judge -- whose agreement with the cardiologists (ICC 0.74, 0.66) matches theirs with each other (0.67). Because each conclusion traces to a cited guideline and is validated against expert cardiologists, it yields decisions a clinician can audit rather than act on blindly -- a step toward use in continuous monitoring.

title: From Semantics to Readout: Mechanistic Understanding of Audio Tokens after Fine-Tuning for Temporal Audio Grounding
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) convey acoustic evidence to language decoders through native audio tokens, yet the internal roles of these tokens remain poorly understood. Using temporal audio grounding as a diagnostic setting, we examine how language-model fine-tuning affects the layerwise semantics, decoder accessibility, and temporal output alignment of native audio-token states through four complementary analyses: query-conditioned token semantics, calibrated token readout, temporal-window probes, and residual-delta erasure during generation. Alongside substantial improvements in temporal localization, semantic analysis of Qwen2.5-Omni shows that latent evidence for queried events is already present before fine-tuning and that the audio tokens most strongly aligned with the queried event appear at similar temporal positions before and after fine-tuning. After fine-tuning, event-related information in audio tokens becomes more accessible to the decoder, especially in early and middle layers, and a cross-checkpoint control shows that this improvement arises primarily from decoder adaptation. Temporal probes show that the base checkpoint already contains recoverable information about annotated windows and that fine-tuning mainly improves alignment with each checkpoint's own predicted temporal support. Residual-delta erasure further shows that removing audio-token updates within predicted windows harms timestamp generation more than removing the same number of randomly selected updates. The same broad improvements in decoder readability and prediction alignment also appear in Qwen2-Audio. Together, these results support a semantics-to-readout account in which grounding fine-tuning helps the decoder read existing event evidence and connect it more reliably to temporal outputs.

title: Specula: Scaling formal specifications for autonomous model checking of system code
abstract: Specula is a push-button agentic system that generates high-quality formal specifications for large, complex system code and uses the specifications for highly effective model checking and bug finding. Specula employs large language model (LLM) based coding agents to autonomously develop TLA+ specifications, including invariants that describe correctness properties of the target system and formal models that describe the system implementation with the right level of abstractions. Specula is fully autonomous and thus eliminates the barrier of applying formal methods to real-world system code (as in traditional human-centric approaches). Meanwhile, Specula addresses limitations of LLM-driven techniques like reward hacking and hallucinations through self-evolving loops that iteratively improve specification quality by enabling the agents to deepen their understanding of system code and its behaviors. We have used Specula to check 48 open-source system projects; Specula found 249 bugs including many deep bugs that are hard to find by existing approaches. Specula has been used by several companies and is maintained at https://github.com/specula-org/Specula.

title: Bekko Embedding: Parameter-Efficient Multilingual Retrieval with Ultra-Compact Encoders
abstract: How small can a competitive multilingual retrieval model be? We present Bekko Embedding: its smallest model, bekko-embedding-v1-a8m, has just under 8M Active Parameters (AP) -- the non-embedding parameters that dominate inference compute -- yet on official MMTEB Multilingual v2 Retrieval (nDCG@10) it scores 56.2, above the multilingual-e5 family and BGE-M3 (40x the AP) in our comparison. The higher-quality bekko-embedding-v1-a25m (just under 25M AP) reaches 57.5, on par with gte-multilingual-base, and Multilingual NanoBEIR (14 languages) confirms the trend. Both models handle inputs of up to 8192 tokens, and on long-input retrieval (NanoLongEmbed) a25m is the strongest dense model in our comparison. The recipe is deliberately simple. We prune the 22-layer multilingual encoder mmBERT-small to 4 / 13 layers and train the pruned models in two stages -- large-scale contrastive learning on about 1.1 billion multilingual pairs from our public corpus, followed by hard-negative fine-tuning with 8192-token long-document negatives -- with a masked contrastive loss whose direction depends on pair type, plus the Matryoshka objective. No teacher distillation is used, and all training completes on a single GPU in about 3 days for a8m. Small AP pays off directly in speed: among the compared models measured under identical conditions, a8m is the fastest on both CPU and GPU -- 1.6x multilingual-e5-small on x86 CPU -- and the fastest on a Raspberry Pi 5. The 384-dimensional output (truncatable to 256/128/64) keeps similarity search and indexing cheap, and row-wise int8 quantization of the vocabulary embedding shrinks the a8m ONNX / OpenVINO build to 124 MiB, which runs in the browser via Transformers.js. To support reproducible research, we release the model weights, the complete stage-1 corpus, and the independently mined stage-2 hard negatives.

title: ContractHIL-HLS: Contract-Aligned Multi-Agent Workflow with Hardware-in-the-Loop Feedback for HLS Design
abstract: This paper presents ContractHIL-HLS, a contract-aligned multi-agent workflow for practical high-level synthesis (HLS) engineering. The workflow makes three contributions. First, it introduces a structured contract as the semantic-alignment and task-execution artifact that translates natural language requirements into explicit interfaces, constraints, validation checks, and rollback rules. Second, it incorporates hardware information into the feedback loop by feeding HLS, Vivado, PYNQ runtime, power, and failure evidence back into generation, thereby extending LLM-assisted HLS from kernel code toward system- and board-level closure. Third, it decomposes agents by semantic lowering and execution tasks rather than by conversational roles: a Contract Agent lowers natural language into the contract, an HTML Agent renders the contract as persistent structured HTML, and a Hardware-in-the-Loop Agent implements and revises the design with measured evidence. We evaluate ContractHIL-HLS in two parts. On 94 locally executable HLS-Eval tasks, the structured contract provides the largest small design gain, improving the estimated single-sample testbench pass rate from 64.0% to 70.2%; the full flow reaches 70.4% pass@1 and 76.6% pass@5. Because HLS-Eval does not exercise board-level design, we also validate ContractHIL-HLS on a board tested ML-KEM/ML-DSA post-quantum cryptography (PQC) secure-message accelerator, where the retained dual-bitstream organization reduces six-message average text runtime from 207.3 ms to 52.4 ms with positive routed WNS on both images while preserving decrypted-message verification. We open-source our work at BJUT-CS316-LAB/ContractHIL-HLS (https://github.com/BJUT-CS316-LAB/ContractHIL-HLS).

title: Hybrid Analysis for Secure MCP Tool Use in LLM Agents
abstract: The rapid development of large language model (LLM) agents has enabled their broad adoption across diverse real-world tasks. To standardize interactions between LLM agents and external environments, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools have emerged as a de facto standard and have been widely integrated into these systems. However, the use of MCP tools also introduces new safety risks, as LLM agents can be induced to perform malicious or unauthorized actions. Although prior work has proposed defenses for securing tool use in LLM agents, most methods rely on static analysis, i.e., inspecting prompts and generated outputs, which limits the defense effectiveness and robustness. To address these limitations, we propose MTGuard, a hybrid analysis-based defense framework designed to safeguard the use of MCP tools in LLM agents by leveraging lifecycle-aware static-dynamic co-analysis. Extensive evaluation demonstrates that MTGuard effectively mitigates multiple categories of harmful tool use across different LLM agents while maintaining performance on benign user tasks.

title: COVENANT: Natural-Language Workflow Compilation for Aligned Agent Execution
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly entrusted with natural-language workflow instructions (e.g., retail-payment policies) that specify not only what outcome to achieve, but also which steps, branches, and tool interactions are permitted. When these instructions are supplied as prompt context, however, the model retains control over both procedure selection and step execution. As interactions accumulate, an agent can skip required steps, take unsupported branches, or execute a valid step with unsupported arguments or effects--a failure mode we call workflow misalignment. In this work, we propose COVENANT, a compiler-and-interpreter architecture for workflow-aligned agent execution. Our key insight is to treat workflow instructions as source programs rather than prompts. COVENANT converts the instructions into a workflow abstract syntax tree (WAST) and lowers it to a workflow control-flow graph (WCFG). At runtime, a controller interprets the WCFG one node at a time, checks each proposal against requirements extracted from the instructions before committing controller state or advancing the graph, and returns diagnostic feedback for repair. To evaluate COVENANT, we use 120 cases from three existing benchmarks, spanning seven workflow scenarios. Compared with state-of-the-art LLM agents, COVENANT improves benchmark success from 50.00% to 83.33% and reduces the workflow-misalignment failure rate from 42.50% to 15.83% (62.75% relative). These results show that COVENANT substantially mitigates workflow misalignment, moving LLM-agent alignment beyond isolated prompt following toward reliable execution of complex and multi-step workflows.

title: A Control System, a Dataset, and a Recipe for Making Frozen LLM Agents Learn a Domain
abstract: Production LLM agents are increasingly assembled from a frozen model wrapped in a harness: a prompt template, a tool set, a memory/retrieval layer, a planning strategy, and a verification policy. Two 2026 systems, Meta-Harness (Lee et al., 2026) and HyperAgents (Meta AI, 2026), show that this harness can itself be optimized or even self-rewritten by an agentic proposer -- at the cost of either an expensive code-search loop or unconstrained self-modifying code, neither of which is auditable or usable with a fully black-box model API. We take a narrower, more constrained position: treat the harness as a small, fixed, human-legible action space and learn a policy over it online with classic sample-efficient reinforcement learning (an $\epsilon$-greedy contextual bandit and REINFORCE), scored against a multi-objective reward (task success, verifier score, policy compliance, cost, latency, and an unsupported-claim penalty). We instantiate this control system with DSPy (Khattab et al., 2024) as both the context assembler and the source of the strongest non-adaptive baseline (a DSPy BootstrapFewShot static prompt), and evaluate it across three verifiable task domains -- tool-use workflows, code generation (HumanEval), and multi-hop retrieval QA (HotpotQA) -- and two model providers (a local Ollama model and AWS Bedrock). We release the harness-control-system code, the cross-domain verifiable task suite, the full trajectory/reward-decomposition logs from training, and a provider-agnostic deployment recipe for applying this to a new organization's domain and verification setup.

title: The Case Against Generation for Retrieval: Discriminative Language Models as Effective Retrievers
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful assets for recommender systems. However, deploying them as generative recommenders or zero-shot rankers at web-scale remains bottlenecked by prohibitive computational overhead and grounding challenges. In this paper, we revitalize the classic, highly efficient two-tower retrieval architecture by adapting LLMs as semantic representation backbones rather than generative engines. We introduce an LLM-native two-tower framework engineered for high-throughput, large-scale retrieval. Our architecture introduces several key innovations: a shared LLM encoder for joint user-item modeling, End-Of-Sentence (EOS) token pooling for compact sequence embedding, cross-dataset transfer learning, knowledge distillation from powerful cross-encoder teachers, and latent reasoning within the user tower. Extensive evaluation across three public benchmarks demonstrates that cross-encoder architecture outperforms current state-of-the-art (SoTA) models, while the efficient two-tower student achieves SoTA-comparable retrieval performance. Furthermore, experiments on internal large-scale production systems yield substantial topline retrieval improvements along with high resilience to model staleness and superior data scaling. Our findings demonstrate that when augmented with modern representation learning, the traditional two-tower paradigm remains an exceptionally competitive and practical solution for industrial retrieval systems.
